name: ip-san-with-mask-bytes-invalid
description: An IPv4 iPAddress SAN MUST be exactly four octets (RFC 5280 §4.2.1.6: the iPAddress alternative is the four-octet IPv4 address or the sixteen-octet IPv6 address). This leaf SAN encodes the *eight-byte* address||mask form used in iPAddress *constraints* — 192.0.2.5 followed by 255.255.255.0 — which is only legal in the nameConstraints extension, never in a SAN. A conforming validator must reject the leaf either because (a) the SAN parses as an unknown-length iPAddress, or (b) it cross-matches the SAN against an active iPAddress constraint (here a permit for 192.0.2.0/24) and finds the lengths incompatible. Bug bait: a validator that accepts a CIDR-shaped iPAddress SAN and either treats the first four bytes as the address (ignoring the trailing mask) or treats the SAN as already being a network specification will silently accept this in violation of §4.2.1.6.
notes: Constructed via unknown_extensions because cryptography.x509.IPAddress always emits a 4- or 16-byte payload for iPAddress SANs.

Distinct from `ip-san-wrong-length-invalid` (3-byte truncated IPv4) — that SAN can't even be interpreted; this one is the inverse failure where the value *looks plausible* but is a constraint shape, not a SAN shape.
